question: Can majority acceptance establish scriptural validity?
premises: One might propose acceptance by the great multitude as the cause of validity.
A great multitude opposed to that position is also possible.
A criterion that can be matched by its opposite lacks firm grounding.
inference: Therefore majority acceptance does not securely establish validity.
plain_english: But if acceptance by the great multitude is taken as the reason for validity, that too is ungrounded, because a great multitude opposed to it can just as well exist.
